Self-reported impulse restraint is easing: 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, a comparison the report characterizes as a modest rebound of intentional indulgence alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance; the measurement period for this figure is not stated.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, reported promotion effectiveness for driving purchase decisions ranked money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) at 75%, percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) at 74%, and buy-one-get-one-free offers at 73%.

Priyanka Bhargav says that today 25% of quick-commerce spending in India comes from mid- to low-affluent consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns, and that these customers are willing to pay a little extra for faster delivery.
Among consumers, 52% report using virtual assistants that automate re-ordering or meal planning at least once a week; separately, 76% want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts.

Agreement among consumers surveyed with wanting Gen AI to provide hyper-personalized content and product/service recommendations based on individual preferences was 58% in November 2024 and 63% in October 2025; each survey had N=12,000 consumers.

In surveys of 12,000 consumers each, the share saying human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage was 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025, an increase of 20 percentage points. At the in-store purchase stage, the corresponding figures were 40% and 66%, an increase of 26 percentage points.

claim_provenance.claim: The reported hypothetical switching conditions are distinct: 74% of consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere, and 71% say they would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication; neither figure measures observed switching.

Separately, in an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, reported promotion effectiveness for driving purchase decisions was 75% for money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25), 74% for percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off), and 73% for buy-one-get-one-free offers.

Together, these findings describe different parts of value response, not a single measure: stated willingness to switch under specified conditions sits alongside reported assessments of promotion effectiveness.

When reviewing value strategy, MarketLense would recommend assessing regular-price switching sensitivity, communication of pack-size or quality reductions, and promotion effectiveness as separate decision questions.

selected_themes: Consumers report separate hypothetical switching intentions: 74% say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere, and 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication; these are stated intentions, not observed switching behavior.

Self-reported impulse restraint is easing: 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, a comparison the report characterizes as a modest rebound of intentional indulgence alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance; the measurement period for this figure is not stated.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, reported promotion effectiveness for driving purchase decisions ranked money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) at 75%, percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) at 74%, and buy-one-get-one-free offers at 73%.

Priyanka Bhargav says that today 25% of quick-commerce spending in India comes from mid- to low-affluent consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns, and that these customers are willing to pay a little extra for faster delivery.
Among consumers, 52% report using virtual assistants that automate re-ordering or meal planning at least once a week; separately, 76% want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts.

Agreement among consumers surveyed with wanting Gen AI to provide hyper-personalized content and product/service recommendations based on individual preferences was 58% in November 2024 and 63% in October 2025; each survey had N=12,000 consumers.

In surveys of 12,000 consumers each, the share saying human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage was 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025, an increase of 20 percentage points. At the in-store purchase stage, the corresponding figures were 40% and 66%, an increase of 26 percentage points.

claim_ledgers.claim_text: Consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere (74%).
Separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication.

The report says 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, and characterizes this as easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).
Among consumers surveyed (N = 12,000 in each survey), 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025 said human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage.

The page reports that 74% of consumers say they would switch brands if they found a lower regular price elsewhere. Separately, it reports that 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication. Both are hypothetical stated intentions, not observed switching behavior.

54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year; the report calls this easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).

Priyanka Bhargav, Head of Insights and Brand Strategy at Flipkart, says that today 25% of quick-commerce spending in India comes from mid- to low-affluent consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns. She adds that these customers are willing to pay a little extra for faster delivery.
52% of consumers use virtual assistants that automate re-ordering or meal planning at least once a week. Separately, 76% want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts.

Among consumers surveyed, agreement with “I want Gen AI to provide hyper-personalized content and product/service recommendations based on my individual preferences” was 58% in November 2024 and 63% in October 2025. Each survey had N=12,000 consumers.

At the in-store customer-support stage, the share of consumers saying human interaction increases loyalty was 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025, an increase of 20 percentage points; each survey had N = 12,000 consumers. At the in-store purchase stage, 40% in November 2024 and 66% in October 2025 said the same, an increase of 26 percentage points; each wave had N=12,000 consumers.

artifacts_payload.expert_comment: The reported hypothetical switching conditions are distinct: 74% of consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere, and 71% say they would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication; neither figure measures observed switching. Separately, in an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, reported promotion effectiveness for driving purchase decisions was 75% for money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25), 74% for percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off), and 73% for buy-one-get-one-free offers. Together, these findings describe different parts of value response, not a single measure: stated willingness to switch under specified conditions sits alongside reported assessments of promotion effectiveness. When reviewing value strategy, MarketLense would recommend assessing regular-price switching sensitivity, communication of pack-size or quality reductions, and promotion effectiveness as separate decision questions.

It states that today 25% of quick-commerce spending comes from mid- to low-affluent consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns, and that these customers are willing to pay a little extra for faster delivery. The preceding quote text says quick commerce is democratizing speed across India, supporting the claim’s India context. The page gives no measurement method or further definition of the spending denominator.

insights_final.metric_public_copy: In self-reports, 54% of consumers in the current report period said they were making fewer impulse purchases, down from 71% last year.
insights_final.now_what: Track impulse purchasing and quantity changes as separate value signals.
insights_final.so_what: The report distinguishes easing impulse restraint from smaller-quantity buying as prices rise.
insights_final.text: 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year; the report calls this easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance.

insights_final.metric_public_copy: In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, 75% rated money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) most effective for driving purchase decisions.

insights_final.so_what: The survey compares how consumers rated promotion formats for driving purchase decisions.
insights_final.text: In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).

insights_final.now_what: When prioritizing in-store service design, assess customer-support and purchase-stage experiences separately.
insights_final.so_what: The reported loyalty measure differs between the customer-support and purchase stages.
insights_final.text: At the in-store customer-support stage, the share of consumers saying human interaction increases loyalty was 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025, an increase of 20 percentage points; each survey had N = 12,000 consumers. At the in-store purchase stage, 40% in November 2024 and 66% in October 2025 said the same, an increase of 26 percentage points; each wave had N=12,000 consumers.

artifacts_payload.linkedin_post:
Consumers report distinct hypothetical switching intentions under two conditions.

74% say they would switch brands if they found a lower regular price elsewhere. Separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication.

These are stated intentions, not observed switching behavior. If reviewing brand value propositions, MarketLense recommends assessing regular-price positioning separately from communication about pack-size or product-quality changes.

summary.executive_summary: Consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere (74%); separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication. The report says 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, and characterizes this as easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%). Among consumers surveyed (N = 12,000 in each survey), 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025 said human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage. MarketLense recommends assessing human interaction at the in-store customer-support stage as part of experience planning.
summary.tldr: Consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere (74%); separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication.

selected_themes: Consumers report separate hypothetical switching intentions: 74% say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere, and 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication; these are stated intentions, not observed switching behavior.

Self-reported impulse restraint is easing: 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, a comparison the report characterizes as a modest rebound of intentional indulgence alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance; the measurement period for this figure is not stated.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, reported promotion effectiveness for driving purchase decisions ranked money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) at 75%, percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) at 74%, and buy-one-get-one-free offers at 73%.

Priyanka Bhargav says that today 25% of quick-commerce spending in India comes from mid- to low-affluent consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns, and that these customers are willing to pay a little extra for faster delivery.
Among consumers, 52% report using virtual assistants that automate re-ordering or meal planning at least once a week; separately, 76% want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts.

Agreement among consumers surveyed with wanting Gen AI to provide hyper-personalized content and product/service recommendations based on individual preferences was 58% in November 2024 and 63% in October 2025; each survey had N=12,000 consumers.

In surveys of 12,000 consumers each, the share saying human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage was 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025, an increase of 20 percentage points. At the in-store purchase stage, the corresponding figures were 40% and 66%, an increase of 26 percentage points.

selected_themes: Consumers report separate hypothetical switching intentions: 74% say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere, and 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication; these are stated intentions, not observed switching behavior.

Self-reported impulse restraint is easing: 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, a comparison the report characterizes as a modest rebound of intentional indulgence alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance; the measurement period for this figure is not stated.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, reported promotion effectiveness for driving purchase decisions ranked money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) at 75%, percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) at 74%, and buy-one-get-one-free offers at 73%.

Priyanka Bhargav says that today 25% of quick-commerce spending in India comes from mid- to low-affluent consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns, and that these customers are willing to pay a little extra for faster delivery.
Among consumers, 52% report using virtual assistants that automate re-ordering or meal planning at least once a week; separately, 76% want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts.

Agreement among consumers surveyed with wanting Gen AI to provide hyper-personalized content and product/service recommendations based on individual preferences was 58% in November 2024 and 63% in October 2025; each survey had N=12,000 consumers.

In surveys of 12,000 consumers each, the share saying human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage was 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025, an increase of 20 percentage points. At the in-store purchase stage, the corresponding figures were 40% and 66%, an increase of 26 percentage points.

planned_themes: Consumers report separate hypothetical switching intentions: 74% say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere, and 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication; these are stated intentions, not observed switching behavior.

Self-reported impulse restraint is easing: 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, a comparison the report characterizes as a modest rebound of intentional indulgence alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance; the measurement period for this figure is not stated.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, reported promotion effectiveness for driving purchase decisions ranked money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) at 75%, percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) at 74%, and buy-one-get-one-free offers at 73%.

claim_ledgers.claim_text: Consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere (74%).
Separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication.

The report says 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, and characterizes this as easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).
Among consumers surveyed (N = 12,000 in each survey), 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025 said human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage.

The page reports that 74% of consumers say they would switch brands if they found a lower regular price elsewhere. Separately, it reports that 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication. Both are hypothetical stated intentions, not observed switching behavior.

54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year; the report calls this easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).

Priyanka Bhargav, Head of Insights and Brand Strategy at Flipkart, says that today 25% of quick-commerce spending in India comes from mid- to low-affluent consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns. She adds that these customers are willing to pay a little extra for faster delivery.
52% of consumers use virtual assistants that automate re-ordering or meal planning at least once a week. Separately, 76% want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts.

Among consumers surveyed, agreement with “I want Gen AI to provide hyper-personalized content and product/service recommendations based on my individual preferences” was 58% in November 2024 and 63% in October 2025. Each survey had N=12,000 consumers.

At the in-store customer-support stage, the share of consumers saying human interaction increases loyalty was 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025, an increase of 20 percentage points; each survey had N = 12,000 consumers. At the in-store purchase stage, 40% in November 2024 and 66% in October 2025 said the same, an increase of 26 percentage points; each wave had N=12,000 consumers.

artifacts.expert_comment: The reported hypothetical switching conditions are distinct: 74% of consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere, and 71% say they would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication; neither figure measures observed switching. Separately, in an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, reported promotion effectiveness for driving purchase decisions was 75% for money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25), 74% for percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off), and 73% for buy-one-get-one-free offers. Together, these findings describe different parts of value response, not a single measure: stated willingness to switch under specified conditions sits alongside reported assessments of promotion effectiveness. When reviewing value strategy, MarketLense would recommend assessing regular-price switching sensitivity, communication of pack-size or quality reductions, and promotion effectiveness as separate decision questions.

insights_final.metric_public_copy: In self-reports, 54% of consumers in the current report period said they were making fewer impulse purchases, down from 71% last year.
insights_final.now_what: Track impulse purchasing and quantity changes as separate value signals.
insights_final.so_what: The report distinguishes easing impulse restraint from smaller-quantity buying as prices rise.
insights_final.text: 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year; the report calls this easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance.

insights_final.metric_public_copy: In surveys of consumers, 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025 said human interaction increases loyalty at the customer-support stage of in-store shopping; each survey had N = 12,000 consumers.
insights_final.now_what: When prioritizing in-store service design, assess customer-support and purchase-stage experiences separately.
insights_final.so_what: The reported loyalty measure differs between the customer-support and purchase stages.
insights_final.text: At the in-store customer-support stage, the share of consumers saying human interaction increases loyalty was 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025, an increase of 20 percentage points; each survey had N = 12,000 consumers. At the in-store purchase stage, 40% in November 2024 and 66% in October 2025 said the same, an increase of 26 percentage points; each wave had N=12,000 consumers.

artifacts.linkedin_post:
Consumers report distinct hypothetical switching intentions under two conditions.

74% say they would switch brands if they found a lower regular price elsewhere. Separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication.

These are stated intentions, not observed switching behavior. If reviewing brand value propositions, MarketLense recommends assessing regular-price positioning separately from communication about pack-size or product-quality changes.

summary.executive_summary: Consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere (74%); separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication. The report says 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, and characterizes this as easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%). Among consumers surveyed (N = 12,000 in each survey), 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025 said human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage. MarketLense recommends assessing human interaction at the in-store customer-support stage as part of experience planning.
summary.tldr: Consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere (74%); separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication.

findings.statement: In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).
findings.text: In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).

verified_facts.statement: In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).

data_dict.commentary: Consumers say they would switch brands for a lower regular price elsewhere (74%); separately, 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication. The report says 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year, and characterizes this as easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%). Among consumers surveyed (N = 12,000 in each survey), 54% in November 2024 and 74% in October 2025 said human interaction increases loyalty at the in-store customer-support stage. MarketLense recommends assessing human interaction at the in-store customer-support stage as part of experience planning.

sections.title: Who should read this report and why?

key_points: Consumers continue to seek deals and cut back on non-essential items, while the chapter frames clear communication and consistent quality as part of fair value.
Price and convenience tend to dominate for frequently purchased, low-involvement categories; brand values and quality can carry more weight for aspirational or longer-lifecycle purchases.
The chapter discusses trust in retail channels through factors such as payment security, data privacy, product authenticity, fulfillment speed, and fair return policies.
sections.summary: The chapter explores how consumers assess value through pricing fairness, transparent policies, product quality, and trust in retail channels. key_points: Around two in five consumers choose lower-cost alternatives, private labels, or smaller quantities to manage budgets, but nearly four in five avoid private labels in performance-critical categories.

sections.summary: This chapter considers how data-driven personalization and technology can support loyalty while respecting privacy and consumer boundaries. It emphasizes that digital convenience does not remove the importance of human support and interaction. fileciteturn1file4turn1file19

key_points: Use digital assistants as engagement channels across discovery, evaluation, and purchase, and adapt interactions to different consumer preferences.

Make AI actions, data use, personalization, and consent clear to consumers; include safeguards that preserve consumer control.
Connect operational AI with accurate pricing, inventory, and customer experience, while embedding fairness and transparency in pricing and loyalty.

It draws on an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers across 12 countries and interviews with consumer products and retail experts. The report examines evolving consumer behavior and implications for consumer products and retail, including value, spending, AI, and technology-enabled loyalty. It draws on a global survey of 12,000 consumers aged 18 and over across Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, the UK, and the US, conducted in October 2025.

scope.scope: The report examines evolving consumer behavior and implications for consumer products and retail, including value, spending, AI, and technology-enabled loyalty. It draws on a global survey of 12,000 consumers aged 18 and over across Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, the UK, and the US, conducted in October 2025.

insights: The page reports that 74% of consumers say they would switch brands if they found a lower regular price elsewhere. Separately, it reports that 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication. Both are hypothetical stated intentions, not observed switching behavior.

54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year; the report calls this easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).

Priyanka Bhargav, Head of Insights and Brand Strategy at Flipkart, says that today 25% of quick-commerce spending in India comes from mid- to low-affluent consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns. She adds that these customers are willing to pay a little extra for faster delivery.
52% of consumers use virtual assistants that automate re-ordering or meal planning at least once a week. Separately, 76% want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts.

findings.statement: In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).
findings.text: In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%).

key_points: 74% of consumers say they would switch brands if they found a lower regular price elsewhere; 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication.
64% view shrinkflation as unfair, while 62% say more attractive deals can make them switch.

sections.summary: The summary presents fairness, quality, spending choices, AI, and human interaction as connected influences on consumer decisions. It previews the report’s findings and implications for consumer products and retail organizations.
sections.title: Executive summary

key_points: The intended audience includes marketing, digital and ecommerce, loyalty, consumer insights, product, category, strategy, pricing, innovation, technology, and data leaders.
The report describes its survey as covering 12,000 consumers aged 18 and over in 12 countries, alongside interviews with consumer products and retail executives.
sections.summary: This section identifies leaders across the consumer products and retail ecosystem who can use the report’s guidance on value, technology, trust, personalization, and consumer decision-making. It also describes the research as a global consumer survey supplemented by executive interviews.
sections.title: Who should read this report and why?

key_points: Consumers continue to seek deals and cut back on non-essential items, while the chapter frames clear communication and consistent quality as part of fair value.
Price and convenience tend to dominate for frequently purchased, low-involvement categories; brand values and quality can carry more weight for aspirational or longer-lifecycle purchases.
The chapter discusses trust in retail channels through factors such as payment security, data privacy, product authenticity, fulfillment speed, and fair return policies.
sections.summary: The chapter explores how consumers assess value through pricing fairness, transparent policies, product quality, and trust in retail channels. It contrasts price-led decisions for frequent or low-involvement purchases with stronger brand or quality considerations in other categories. fileciteturn1file1turn3file15
sections.title: Value redefined: where fairness and quality intersect

key_points: Around two in five consumers choose lower-cost alternatives, private labels, or smaller quantities to manage budgets, but nearly four in five avoid private labels in performance-critical categories.
The chapter describes a hybrid approach: trading down in some categories while retaining spending in others, including health-related purchases.
Three in four consumers identify money-off discounts as the most motivating promotion type, followed by percent-off and buy-one-get-one offers.
Seven in ten say small indulgences help manage financial stress.
sections.summary: This chapter describes consumers balancing deliberate saving with selective treats, and explains how category, reliability, and emotional satisfaction shape those choices. It also considers deal preferences and delivery convenience. fileciteturn1file6turn2file11
sections.title: Careful spending meets intentional indulgence

key_points: 52% of consumers use virtual assistants that automate reordering or meal planning at least once a week, while only one in five is willing to pay for such services.
76% want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts, and 71% are worried about how generative AI uses their information.
The executive summary reports that 35% have already purchased through social platforms such as Instagram or YouTube.
sections.summary: The chapter examines AI’s expanding role in product discovery, shopping assistance, and purchasing, alongside consumer expectations for transparency and control. It discusses how organizations can adapt product information and engagement for AI-mediated journeys. fileciteturn1file8turn2file11
sections.title: AI - The consumer’s trusted guide

key_points: 63% want generative AI to provide hyper-personalized content, and 65% say technology has reduced stress in their shopping routines.
For in-store customer support, 74% said human interaction increased loyalty in October 2025, up from 54% in November 2024; at the purchase stage, the corresponding figures were 66% and 40%.
The chapter presents technology as a way to enhance service and personalization, not as a substitute for the emotional value of human interaction.
sections.summary: This chapter considers how data-driven personalization and technology can support loyalty while respecting privacy and consumer boundaries. It emphasizes that digital convenience does not remove the importance of human support and interaction. fileciteturn1file4turn1file19
sections.title: Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries

key_points: Use digital assistants as engagement channels across discovery, evaluation, and purchase, and adapt interactions to different consumer preferences.
Develop machine-readable, current product information and optimize brand presence for AI-mediated recommendations.
Make AI actions, data use, personalization, and consent clear to consumers; include safeguards that preserve consumer control.
Connect operational AI with accurate pricing, inventory, and customer experience, while embedding fairness and transparency in pricing and loyalty.
sections.summary: This section translates the findings into actions for consumer products and retail organizations, spanning intelligent engagement, operational AI, and purpose-led transformation. Recommendations emphasize clear data and product information, consumer control, fairness, and trustworthy experiences. fileciteturn2file0turn1file10
sections.title: What should CPR organizations do differently?

key_points: Organizations should make value legible and combine intelligence, transparency, and purpose.
The report recommends introducing automation gradually with safeguards and treating loyalty as a two-way relationship.
sections.summary: The conclusion argues that consumer value now combines price and quality with fairness, transparency, emotional reassurance, and access to useful technology. It calls for a cohesive strategy that builds trust through responsible AI, clear pricing, consumer agency, and human-centered experiences.

In an October 2025 survey of 12,000 consumers, money-off offers (e.g., $5 off $25) were rated most effective for driving purchase decisions (75%), followed by percent-off offers (e.g., 20% off) (74%) and buy-one-get-one-free offers (73%). insights: The page reports that 74% of consumers say they would switch brands if they found a lower regular price elsewhere. Separately, it reports that 71% would switch if pack sizes or product quality were reduced without clear communication. Both are hypothetical stated intentions, not observed switching behavior.

54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases in the current report period, down from 71% last year; the report calls this easing impulse restraint and a modest rebound of “intentional indulgence” alongside persistent deal-seeking. Separately, as prices rise, around half of consumers (49%) are buying smaller quantities, which the report characterizes as consumption control rather than complete avoidance.

of consumers view ‘shrinkflation’1 as an unfair

Careful spending meets intentional

Consumers are becoming more deliberate about 
how they save and where they treat themselves. 
AI-enabled shopping, heightened expectations 
of fairness and transparency, and meaningful 
human interaction at key moments are reshaping 
consumer decision-making in a new era of 
empowered consumer decision making. As AI 
becomes more deeply woven into everyday 
choices, shoppers are rewriting what they 
consider acceptable, valuable, and worth paying 
for. Expectations are sharper, tolerance is lower, 
and the definition of value has expanded beyond 
price. This report explores how AI, trust, and 
emotion are reshaping what consumers perceive 
as worth their time, money, and attention

percent off and buy one get one offers. Impulse 
restraint is also easing 54% say they are making 
fewer impulse purchases, down from 71% last 
year, signaling a modest rebound of ‘intentional 
indulgence’ alongside persistent deal- seeking.
Trust in channels matters. Two in three consumers 
believe ecommerce offers fair prices, with thrift 
and discount formats close behind. Emotional 
release also plays a role. Seven in ten say small 
indulgences help manage financial stress, 
showing that value blends rational savings with 
emotional satisfaction.
AI - The consumer’s trusted guide
AI-driven tools are becoming central to how 
shoppers navigate the marketplace. Chatbots 
are now widely used for service and personalized 
follow up, and agentic AI is moving into routine 
tasks. Almost half of consumers (52%) use virtual 
assistants that automate re-ordering or meal 
planning at least once a week, though only one 
in five is willing to pay a monthly subscription or 
a one-time payment. Control remains essential. 
Seventy six percent want the ability to set clear 
rules for when an assistant acts. Concerns about 
transparency continue, with 71 percent worried 
about how generative AI uses their information. 
Awareness of synthetic influencers is widespread 
at 66 percent, yet trust remains low at 52 percent. 
Two thirds of consumers expect brands to disclose 
AI generated advertising. Social commerce is 
growing quickly, and 35 percent have already 
purchased through platforms like Instagram 
or YouTube.
Technological convenience with a 
human touch drives loyalty
Consumers want efficiency, relevance, and 
emotional connection to coexist. Sixty three 
percent want generative AI to provide hyper 
personalized content, and 65 percent feel 
technology has reduced stress in their shopping 
routines. Yet human support remains essential. 
More than seven in ten consumers value in person 
assistance when dealing with complex purchases 
or resolving service issues. Preference for human 
assistance has risen sharply, with seventy four 
percent valuing support during in-store customer 
service and sixty six percent during the purchase 
stage, up from 54 percent and 40 percent last year. 
To win consumer loyalty brands must focus on fair 
value and dependable experiences such as clear 
pricing, consistent product quality, and a balanced 
mix of digital convenience and human support.
